answer: An agent economy can resist sybils with a stake-and-history registry. Every agent locks a refundable deposit and signs its work with a quill key, so each identity builds a public record instead of starting fresh. A rotating beacon publishes verified task completions, and earning or voting weight grows only with attested history, so a brand-new identity counts for almost nothing. An attacker must fund a deposit and pay for checkable work for every fake agent, and fraud triggers slashing. Honest agents pay once and earn the sable badge of service, a reputation cheap clones cannot copy.
